name: Gut health protocols (gut-skin axis)

lead: Gut health protocols combine steps such as removing suspected trigger foods, adding probiotics or fermented foods and eating more fibre, with the aim of clearer skin through the gut. They are discussed in skin communities under the label gut-skin axis.

The chain: gut bacteria and their metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids, are proposed to affect immune and inflammatory signalling that could reach the skin. Gut-brain axis research relies heavily on animal models and small human studies, and its associations are considered correlational rather than causal. Elimination diets are an established diagnostic tool for food allergy, and probiotics for acne are described as preliminary research. No trials of the bundled protocols for skin appearance were found.

paras: People usually run it as a multi-step routine: cut suspected trigger foods for a period, add fermented foods or a probiotic, raise fibre intake, then reintroduce foods one at a time to see what the skin does. Users report judging results over several weeks.

Elimination diets need to stay nutritionally complete, and strict forms are generally not recommended in pregnancy. Probiotics are generally considered safe, but rare bloodstream infections have occurred in immunocompromised people.

chain: Eliminating triggers, adding probiotics and fibre
angle.text: Users bundle food elimination, probiotics, fermented foods and fibre to clear skin through the gut. The idea is that healthier gut microbes calm the immune and inflammatory signalling that reaches the skin. The gut-skin links are mostly associations.

lead: Gut health protocols for skin typically bundle elimination of suspected trigger foods with probiotics, fermented foods and fibre. The shared premise is a gut-skin axis in which gut microbes influence skin through immune and metabolic signalling.

Wikipedia's account of the related gut-brain axis states that much of the research is in animals, human studies are small, and links to conditions are considered correlational rather than causal; it does not discuss skin [1]. Elimination diets are an established diagnostic tool for food allergy, and probiotics for acne are described as preliminary research [2][3].
No studies of combined gut-health protocols for skin appearance were found.
infobox: Gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids

paras: An elimination diet removes suspected foods for roughly two weeks to two months and then reintroduces them one at a time [2]. Probiotics are live microorganisms for which benefits are strain-specific, and acne uses are described as preliminary [3].

No studies found on combined gut-health protocols for skin. Wikipedia notes gut-microbiome research relies heavily on animal models and small human cohorts, and that probiotic therapies face difficulty colonising the gut [1].

lore.intro: Gut-skin protocols are discussed as a root-cause approach to acne and complexion.

claims.claim: Fixing the gut clears the skin
